shots.line: In this town, everyone's out partying on a Friday night. People are getting dressed, making plans, and probably making some questionable decisions.
And then there's me.
Making questionable decisions of my own.
Welcome to recruiting season as a computer science student. Where you spend hours perfecting your resume just to manually enter everything that's already on it.
And after answering why I'm passionate about working for a company I discovered 15 minutes ago, I finally submit my application.
Great.
Anyway, next.
But applying is only half the battle. Apparently, to become a software engineer, I need to know how to reverse a linked list while someone watches me struggle in real time.
I'll spend 40 minutes solving a problem, look at the solution, and realize it could've been done in six lines.
That little green accepted screen is probably the only thing keeping me going at this point.
And occasionally, after sending out an ungodly number of applications, someone actually wants to talk to me.
Which means days of preparing, practicing technical questions, and rehearsing how to introduce myself without sounding like I've rehearsed how to introduce myself.
Hi, I'm currently a junior studying computer science at Penn State...
Hi, I'm currently a junior...
Hi...
And just like that, it's back to waiting.
Sometimes I wonder if I'm taking all of this a little too seriously.
I'm in college. I'm supposed to be making memories, going out, and enjoying these years before I have actual responsibilities.
But at the same time, there's a life I really want to build for myself. And unfortunately, wanting it isn't enough.
The weirdest part is putting in all this work without knowing when, or even if, it's going to pay off.
I don't have everything figured out. Half the time, I feel like I'm just making it up as I go.
But every application, every problem, and every interview is another chance to get a little closer to where I want to be.
Maybe next weekend.
